title: Classical inference — ANOVA, descriptive statistics, hypothesis tests (anova + descriptive + hypothesis)
procedure: First-time validation of the corpus's three grouped correctness-dominant modules, across the WHOLE public surface, at 4.6.11 (a patch that fixed five R-convention divergences found at 4.6.10), re-validated at 5.0.0 (a rename-only release over the blessed 4.6.11 line; statistically identical, every G1/G2 number reproduces 4.6.11 bit-for-bit — the 5.0 API renames prop_test/var_test null args to null_value, chisq_test goodness-of-fit probs to expected_probs, and prop_test trials to n_trials). These are DETERMINISTIC, closed-form modules: almost every quantity has a closed-form statistic and (often) an exact p-value, so the bar is machine precision / exact, not an optimizer tier, and the work is exact per-function convention-matching against R's defaults. descriptive: describe/summary, cor (pearson/spearman/kendall tau-b), cov, var (n-1), quantile (all 9 R types, default type 7; skew/kurt = e1071 type 2). hypothesis: t_test (Welch default, pooled/paired/one-sample), chisq_test (Yates 2x2 default + GoF), fisher_test (exact hypergeometric + conditional-MLE odds ratio), wilcox_test (exact/normal-approx switch, Hodges-Lehmann CI), ks_test (one/two-sample), prop_test, var_test, p_adjust (all 8 methods). anova: anova_oneway (Type I), anova (Type II default = car::Anova, + I/III), anova_posthoc (TukeyHSD), anova_rm (within-F, Mauchly + GG/HF vs afex), levene_test (Brown-Forsythe, center=median default). Validated against R on identical float64 inputs from the central HDF5 store, with scipy.stats as an independent third reference where R and scipy differ on a convention. NO GPU path is warranted (closed-form scalars / O(n) reductions, no normal-equations Gram; CF-1 is N/A) and none is manufactured.
algorithms: descriptive (deterministic, machine-precision vs R). var/cov use the n-1 denominator; cor supports pearson (default), spearman (rank), and kendall tau-b with the tie correction; quantile implements all 9 R types with default type 7 (the H&F taxonomy); describe/summary expose mean/sd/var/median/min/max plus skewness and kurtosis matched to e1071 type 2 (bias-adjusted). Every quantity matches R to machine precision on identical fp64 inputs.

hypothesis — parametric (deterministic). t_test defaults to Welch (var.equal=FALSE) with the Welch-Satterthwaite df; pooled/paired/one-sample selectable; two-sided default. var_test is the F ratio test. prop_test is the score/chi-square test with Yates continuity correction (default TRUE), and its two-sample CI applies R's capped correction min(0.5, |p1-p2|/(1/n1+1/n2)). chisq_test applies the Yates correction by default for 2x2, warns when expected counts < 5, and supports goodness-of-fit vs independence.

hypothesis — exact / rank (deterministic). fisher_test computes the exact hypergeometric p-value and the conditional-MLE odds ratio + CI by noncentral-hypergeometric root-find (2x2; r x c p-value by seeded Monte-Carlo simulation, disclosed in the method string). wilcox_test switches exact <-> normal-approximation (exact for small n without ties; ties -> normal approx + warning), and computes the Hodges-Lehmann CI by exact order-statistic inversion (qsignrank/qwilcox on the sorted Walsh averages/differences) or tie-corrected normal-approx inversion, dropping zero differences for the signed-rank test -- matching R exactly. ks_test does one-sample (exact Kolmogorov, ties warning) and two-sample. p_adjust implements holm (default), hochberg, hommel, bonferroni, BH, BY, none.

anova (deterministic given SS type). anova_oneway computes sequential Type I; anova defaults to Type II (car::Anova) with Type I/III selectable, validated against the MATCHING R type (an unbalanced two-way design confirms Type I/II/III diverge and each matches its R counterpart -- no silent SS-type substitution). anova_posthoc/tukey uses the studentized-range q with family-wise CIs (TukeyHSD). levene_test transforms to |y - center(group)| then runs one-way ANOVA, center='median' by default (Brown-Forsythe, car's default).

anova_rm (repeated measures, deterministic). Within-subject F on orthonormal Helmert contrasts, Mauchly's sphericity W with R's second-order (Box) corrected p-value (p = Pr1 + w2*(Pr2 - Pr1), Pr2 at df+4), and Greenhouse-Geisser / Huynh-Feldt epsilons (HF reported capped at 1). Validated against afex::aov_ez / stats::mauchly.test.

reference.name: R stats + car + afex + e1071 + TukeyHSD
reference.what: Each function is validated against its canonical R reference on identical float64 inputs (each dataset is dumped from the central HDF5 store and analysed by both engines): var/cov/cor/quantile/describe vs base stats (+ e1071 for skew/kurt); t/chisq/fisher/wilcox/ks/prop/var.test/p.adjust vs base stats; anova_oneway vs anova(lm) Type I; anova vs car::Anova(type='II'/'III'); levene_test vs car::leveneTest; anova_posthoc vs TukeyHSD; anova_rm vs afex::aov_ez. The reference METHOD and convention are matched per function (Welch t-test, quantile type 7, cor tau-b, chisq correct=TRUE, wilcox exact-when-small, Levene center=median, anova Type II) -- never a different estimator.
reference.third_reference: scipy.stats (pearsonr/spearmanr/kendalltau, ttest_ind, skew) used to adjudicate where R and scipy differ on a convention; R's convention is pinned.

tolerances.g1_statistics_and_pvalues: Machine precision (<= ~2e-13) on every test statistic and every default exact/asymptotic p-value on valid input.
tolerances.g1_fisher_cmle_root_find: Conditional-MLE odds ratio and its CI agree with R to ~5-7 digits on well-conditioned tables (internal noncentral-hypergeometric root-find); on an extreme flat-tail table only the exact p-value is asserted.
tolerances.g1_fisher_rxc_monte_carlo: The r x c Fisher p-value is a seeded Monte-Carlo simulation (disclosed), compared to R's exact p within Monte-Carlo error (~3.6e-3 at B=1e4), not machine precision.
tolerances.g1_wilcox_approx_ci: The two approximate (tie/large-n) wilcox CIs are inverted by root-finding and agree with R to R's own uniroot tolerance (~1e-4); the exact-regime CIs are machine-exact.
tolerances.g2_fidelity_fail_loud: Invalid / dimension-mismatched / out-of-range input raises ValidationError (A6); no silent default. quantile probs outside [0,1] raise (matching R); var of a single observation returns nan (= R NA).
tolerances.g2_warning_fidelity: The chi-square small-expected-count warning, the wilcox ties->normal-approx warning, and the one-sample KS ties warning reproduce R's wording; the exact->approx and Fisher-simulation switches are disclosed in the method string.
tolerances.g3_performance_cpu: CPU parity with R on O(n) reductions at n=1e6 (compute-vs-compute). No GPU path (closed-form scalars / small reductions, no normal-equations Gram; CF-1 N/A) -- documented, not manufactured.

limitations: No open findings. Five R-convention divergences were found at 4.6.10 (F1 wilcox HL CI; F2 prop two-sample CI continuity cap; F3 one-sample KS ties warning; F4 Mauchly second-order p correction; F5 quantile fail-loud on out-of-range probs) and ALL were fixed and re-validated in the 4.6.11 patch this report blesses (RIGOR R18 bless precondition: no open fixable finding); the bless carries forward unchanged to 5.0.0 (rename-only over 4.6.11). No test statistic or default p-value on valid input was ever wrong.
The fisher_test r x c p-value is a seeded Monte-Carlo simulation by default (R's default is exact, often intractable for r x c); disclosed in the method string and reproducible when the seed is set.
